title: Perimeter observability mesh for tenant-bounded sampling and schema enforcement
creator: Elena Morris
description:
Summary: Implement a perimeter observability mesh (collector+ingress layer) that enforces per-tenant sampling policies, lightweight telemetry schema validation, and tenant-bounded rate shaping for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to stop noisy tenants from degrading telemetry pipelines and downstream dashboards while preserving high-fidelity traces/metrics for SLA-critical customers.

Background: Current ingest and collector components accept unbounded telemetry from tenant environments in Dedicated/VPC clusters. We have recurring issues where one tenant spikes trace volume (large batch replays, noisy SDKs) and increases processing latency and costs for other tenants. Existing approaches (simple sampling at SDK or global sampler) are insufficient because they either lose important spans for high-SLA tenants or allow noisy telemetry through.

Scope: This ticket covers design and implementation of an in-cluster perimeter mesh that sits at ingress (edge-forwarder or sidecar aggregator) and enforces: 1) per-tenant rate limits and soft throttling for traces/metrics/logs; 2) tenant-aware adaptive sampling profiles (preserve high-fidelity for high-SLA routes); 3) lightweight schema validation/enrichment to drop clearly malformed payloads and annotate dropped events; 4) histogram-based shapers to protect overall ingestion latency. The mesh must be configurable via Console policies, support offline/private deployments (air-gapped), and integrate with existing collector components and our rollout/fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Perimeter mesh deployed in a Dedicated staging cluster and applied to at least 3 tenants with distinct sampling profiles
Per-tenant sampling policy can be updated via Console and policy changes apply within 2 minutes without pod restarts
Noisy tenant spike test: during a synthetic 10x trace volume spike from tenant A, overall collector tail latency increases by <10% for other tenants
Schema enforcement drops malformed spans and annotates drop events with reason codes visible in the diagnostics dashboard
Integration tests for on-prem installer: mesh components install with offline bundle and do not require outbound internet connectivity
E2E dashboards: telemetry ingest rate, per-tenant dropped events, sampling ratio, and tail-latency charts populated in Console
tasks: Design: finalize mesh architecture (sidecar vs edge-forwarder) and failure semantics
Proto: implement a minimal adaptive sampler with per-tenant configs and histogram shaper
Schema: implement lightweight validator for OTLP/JSON payloads and drop/mutate rules
Console: add policy UI and API endpoints for per-tenant sampling and drop rules
E2E: synthetic load harness to inject tenant spikes and verify isolation
On-prem: package mesh as part of offline installer and add upgrade tests
Docs: runbook for operator actions when a tenant becomes noisy and troubleshooting guide
comments: 2025-02-19 - Elena Morris: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. We decided to prototype an edge-forwarder path first to avoid sidecar scaling complexity. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Perimeter+Mesh+Design

2025-02-25 - Rajiv Singh: Initial prototype pushed to feature branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/371. Prototype implements per-tenant token bucket and a sampler that preserves top N root spans per minute.

2025-03-01 - SRE (Priya Kapoor): Ran tenant-spike test in staging. Observed a 6% tail-latency increase for non-spiking tenants. Logged results to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/obs/mesh-staging-tenant-spike

2025-03-03 - Security (Marco Liu): Requested a short threat model for how mesh handles malformed payloads and KMS access for tenant identifiers. Assigned back to engineering to document KMS usage in on-prem flows.

2025-03-04 - Rajiv Singh: Added fallback semantics to route to a 'degraded-collector' when the mesh cannot validate schema for >50% of payloads to avoid blocking critical telemetry. Added unit tests for fallback path. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/389
